stories.headline: Democrats win control of both chambers of Congress

sources.body:
The Maine Senate race now leans Democrat, CBS rates.

The contest between incumbent Republican Senator Susan Collins and Democrat Troy Jackson was previously marked a toss up.
sources.headline: Democrats win Senate and control of US Congress after historic victories in Republican strongholds

sources.body:
The outcome is widely seen as a rebuke to Trump’s Republican Party, which took control of the upper chamber in the 2024 election.

The Democratic Party has regained control of the upper chamber of the United States Congress in the 2026 midterm elections, according to Associated Press news agency projections.

The Senate was called in the party’s favour late on Tuesday night, marking a dramatic shift in legislative power.

Democrats needed a net gain of four seats in the 100-member chamber to wrest control from the Republicans.

Some of those gains were dramatic. In South Carolina, for instance, Democrat Annie Andrews, a paediatrician, took a seat held by Republican Darline Graham, the sister of the late longtime Senator Lindsey Graham. The last time a Democrat won a Senate seat in the state was 1998.

Neighbouring North Carolina saw a similar flip, with Democrat Roy Cooper, a former governor, beating his Republican rival Michael Whatley.

In Texas, a Republican stronghold, Democrat James Talarico, a state legislator and seminary student, delivered an upset against state Attorney General Ken Paxton. The last time a Democrat won a statewide election in Texas was 1994.

Democrat Sherrod Brown also defeated incumbent Republican Senator Jon Husted in Ohio, flipping that seat as well. And in Kansas, Adam Hamilton, the Democratic pastor of a megachurch, beat another sitting senator, Republican Roger Marshall.

In the outgoing 119th Congress, Republicans hold a 53-seat majority. The Democrats have 45 seats, with two independents in their caucus.

With Tuesday’s results, Democrats have secured at least 51 seats, enough to take the majority, with a handful of races still being counted.

The outcome is also set to end the Republican “trifecta” achieved in the 2024 election, when the party won control of the three main levers of power in Washington, DC: the Senate, the House of Representatives and the presidency.

The Senate was projected to be harder to flip than the House in Tuesday’s midterm elections, given the smaller number of seats on the ballot.

Senate terms last six years, unlike the two-year terms of members of the House of Representatives. And elections for senators are staggered, meaning that only about a third of all Senate seats are voted on at a time.

This midterm election cycle saw 35 Senate races: 33 regular elections and two special elections, in Ohio and Florida. Those two states were left with Senate vacancies when Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio joined President Donald Trump’s second administration in 2025.

At least seven Senate races on Tuesday were considered key toss-ups. They included contests in Alaska, Iowa, Kansas, Maine, Ohio, Texas and Michigan.

States like Texas and Kansas, however, rarely fall within the toss-up category, as they are considered Republican strongholds. The last time a Democratic senator was elected in Kansas was 1932.

“How did this happen? How did a Democrat win in Kansas, a deeply red state, for the first time in nearly a century, especially in a state where only 25 percent of the people are Democrats?” Senator-elect Hamilton said in his victory speech.
sources.headline: Democratic Party flips US Senate in 2026 midterm elections

sources.body: Democrats won control of the Senate in the US midterm elections Tuesday, with initial results showing the party securing shock victories in Texas, Ohio, North and South Carolina, Kansas and Iowa.
sources.headline: Key US Senate results: Democrats win upper chamber with victories in Texas and Iowa

stories.headline: Democrats win Texas Senate and governor races in a statewide breakthrough

sources.body: AUSTIN — Democrats’ vision of a blue Texas is finally here. James Talarico has been elected a U.S. senator and Gina Hinojosa as governor, the first Democrats to win either office in more than a generation. The four other statewide candidates are leading as ballots continue to be counted. Democrats further down the ballot are leading some red districts, changing the complexion of the state legislature, congressional delegation and courts. “It’s something that I haven’t seen in decades, that none of us have seen in decades,” said former Texas House Speaker Joe Straus, a moderate Republican. It’s an outcome that even the most bullish Democrats didn’t dare enunciate in the late days of the election. But as results have poured in Tuesday night, the party is outpacing its expectations across the country’s second most populous state amidst a national romp. Both Hinojosa’s and Talarico’s victory margins came by running up vote counts in Texas’ deep-blue urban centers and while also leading in the largest Republican-led county in the country, Tarrant County. They reversed Republican gains across the Latino-heavy Rio Grande Valley region, an ancestrally Democratic area that had swung hard to the right in recent years. Democratic Rep. Vicente Gonzalez romped to a near-20 point victory in a seat Republicans drew to favor them during last year’s redrawing of the state’s House map, ousting a top Republican recruit who campaigned alongside Speaker Mike Johnson to begin election day. It amounts to a set of remarkable results in a state that hasn’t elected a Democrat to the U.S. Senate since 1988 and to the governor’s mansion since 1990. In recent cycles, Democrats have tried and failed to flip the state in presidential and U.S. Senate contests but have been largely uncompetitive for state offices. But Tuesday’s blue wave slammed into Texas particularly hard, as it combined frustrations over the economy, immigration enforcement, data centers and corruption with a collapse of Trump’s 2024 coalition. “We reminded voters that Republicans have been in charge in Texas for 30 years. That every problem we have, was caused by Republicans,” Michelle Lowe Solis, chair of the Bexar County Democratic Party. “They aren’t going to fix the problems, they caused them.” As votes continue to be counted, Democrats appear poised to blunt the impact of Republicans’ attempted gerrymander, likely sweeping the Rio Grande Valley congressional seats while holding onto another San Antonio-area district drawn to favor Republicans. In state Supreme Court races, they lead in all four seats up for grabs, potentially turning a 9-0 conservative majority into a 5-4 split. Among the first 36 state house races called by the Associated Press, 34 have gone to Democrats and just two to Republicans.“Voters aren't dumb,” said Rep. Linda Sanchez (D-Calif.), who chairs the Congressional Hispanic Caucus’ BOLD PAC. “Even though the Republicans have tried to cheat with the series of gerrymanders, that has, I think, only made voters in those areas more willing to participate.” Talarico’s and Hinojosa’s victories will be felt nationally. Texas Democrats, who have long asked for national money and resources in a state where elections are costly, now have a test case of how to win. And it will bolster their arguments that their state, with 40 electoral votes, should be treated as a presidential battleground. Ali Bianco and Jonathan Martin contributed reporting.
sources.headline: Democrats sweep Texas

sources.body:
James Talarico has won the United States Senate race in Texas, the first time a Democrat has won state office since 1994.

Tuesday’s victory marks a seismic shift in Texas , which has become a standard-bearer for the Republican Party’s staunch conservative policies.

The win comes after a primary intervention by President Donald Trump, which saw him endorse scandal-ridden Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton over Republican Senate candidate John Cornyn.

But Paxton failed to generate enthusiasm, even among his party, despite record-breaking spending, topping more than half a billion dollars.

The largest share came from billionaire donor Elon Musk, who spent at least $212m supporting Paxton.

Musk’s SpaceX company is based in Texas. He has also spent heavily across the country, with Democrats expected to investigate Musk’s role as head of the federal cost-cutting panel DOGE if they take control of Congress.

“It’s historic,” said Taylor Bell, a 27-year-old law student, who attended an election watch party in Houston.

“Hopefully, we see money coming back to the people of Texas, and not more of the same we’ve seen – well, my whole life at this point.”

US Congressman Christian Menefee, a Democrat who represents Houston, told those gathered that “tonight, Texas has restored the hope of a nation”.

“Tonight, I believe firmly that we can accomplish anything in this country if we just stand together and we fight back against hate and bigotry,” he said.

Yvonne Nunga, a 29-year-old who works in IT, said: “The younger generation and all the people who want a better future came out and made their voices heard.

“This party, this fight right now, is not about left or right. It’s about top versus bottom, and I’m so glad that we have candidates that are making this a pivotal point in their messaging,” she added.

“The current politics of the current administration is not working for the people. It’s not for the people, by the people; it’s for the billionaires bought by the billionaires.”

Tuesday also saw the surprise victory of gubernatorial Democratic challenger Gina Hinojosa, whose challenge had been considered a long shot even into the final days of the race.

Hinojosa has become the first Latino governor in the history of Texas, despite Latinos making up 40 percent of the state’s population.

Alejandra Peimbert, a regional communications director for Hinojosa’s campaign, said the victory should be seen as a rebuke to the hardline immigration policies enacted during 10 years under outgoing Governor Greg Abbott.

Abbott has cooperated closely with the Trump administration in its mass deportation campaign, spearheading policies that saw local law enforcement officials conduct immigration enforcement.

“I think the Latino community and our vote has been underestimated by politicians constantly,” Peimbert told Al Jazeera.

“The economy is so bad, and the horrendous things that ICE has done to our community, tearing apart families… I think my community finally had enough,” she added, referring to the Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency.
sources.headline: Talarico wins Texas Senate race, ending decades of Republican dominance

stories.headline: Keisha Lance Bottoms becomes the first Black woman elected governor of a US state

sources.body:
Bottoms, who formerly advised ex-President Joe Biden, beat Republican Rick Jackson.

Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms has made history as the first Black woman elected governor of a US state, according to Associated Press news agency projections.

The former Atlanta mayor emerged victorious in Georgia over her billionaire opponent, Republican Rick Jackson, who spent more than $200m of his personal fortune in an attempt to succeed the popular outgoing Republican governor, Brian Kemp.

Bottoms, a former adviser to US President Joe Biden, was propelled to victory in part by the state’s significant Black voting bloc, which turned out in large numbers during early voting.

During the campaign, she faced Republican attempts to characterise her time as mayor as a crime-ridden decline for the state’s largest city.

“It’s a longstanding playbook to paint Atlanta as this big bad place,” Bottoms told the Associated Press news agency.

Bottoms’ win marks the third consecutive time that Georgia Democrats have nominated a Black woman for governor. Stacey Abrams lost in 2018 and 2022 to Kemp, who is leaving office in January after eight years due to term limits.
sources.headline: Keisha Lance Bottoms makes history as first Black woman elected US governor

stories.headline: Iran rejects US response to Hormuz proposal as Trump confirms strikes

sources.body:
Indirect talks continue as Trump says US military struck an Iranian anti-aircraft facility on Tuesday.

Iran has called the US response to its seven conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz “unconvincing” as US President Donald Trump confirmed launching strikes on an Iranian island near the strategic waterway.

The developments on Tuesday came as Qatar stepped up diplomatic efforts to avert a renewed war between the US and Iran and as another oil tanker was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz.

The indirect talks centre on an Iranian proposal to reopen the waterway over two days, if the US meets Tehran’s seven demands, including the lifting of sanctions and ending a US naval blockade.

Despite reports of progress in recent days, Mohsen Rezaei, the secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, said on Tuesday that Washington’s response had fallen short.

“America’s response to Iran’s rights and demands was not convincing, and they must fully and explicitly address Iran’s seven conditions and act upon them,” he wrote on X.

“Only in this case will the Strait of Hormuz be reopened.”

His post came after Majed al-Ansari, a spokesperson for Qatar’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, said that talks were continuing and that both sides “remain committed to the negotiation process”.

He said Qatar was facilitating the “real-time exchange of proposals between” the US and Iran.

In Washington, DC, Trump confirmed the US had struck Iran early on Tuesday, telling Fox News that the strikes had targeted an anti-aircraft facility.

He described the operation as a “minor attack” and said it “wasn’t war”.

“They built an anti-aircraft facility. It took them about two months. We watched it get built. As soon as it was completed, we hit it last night,” he said.

Iranian media said the strikes hit Qeshm Island in the Gulf near the Strait of Hormuz. Earlier in the day, US officials told US media that the strikes had been “defensive” and followed Iranian fire at an American aircraft.

The strikes came as US media, citing US officials, reported that Central Command had prepared plans for strikes that could begin as early as Wednesday, after the midterm elections, when three American aircraft carriers would be in the region.

The crucial elections could cost Trump’s Republicans control of both the House and the Senate, and fears have grown that Trump could carry out a threatened attack on Iran once the vote is over.

US media have previously reported that the planned campaign would be short and intense.

Trump meanwhile repeated warnings of further military action on Tuesday, saying, “I’m not looking to … kill lots of people” and “If we have to, we’ll have to.”

In an earlier interview with the Financial Times, he suggested he was content with the state of the stand-off with Iran. “We seem to be getting everything we want,” the paper quoted him as saying in a six-minute telephone interview.

Iran’s supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, meanwhile ordered the military at the weekend to respond to any threat immediately and without geographical limits, and to update its list of targets.
sources.headline: Iran says US reply to Hormuz plan ‘unconvincing’; Trump confirms strikes

stories.headline: South Africans vote in local elections amid anger over failing services

sources.body:
Party expected to get less than a third of the vote amid frustration over water outages and power cuts

The African National Congress is on course for a bruising result in South Africa’s local elections on Wednesday as voters go to the polls amid deep discontent over water outages, power cuts and crumbling infrastructure.

The former liberation movement, which Nelson Mandela led to power in 1994 at the end of apartheid as South Africa’s first black president, is still likely to be the largest party. However, polls show it getting less than a third of the vote, down from 45.6% at the last municipal elections in 2021 and 40.2% in 2024’s national elections .

Vote fragmentation means the ANC could still end up leading many city coalition governments while losing control of others.

Unstable coalitions are already a feature of many of South Africa’s 257 municipalities, and analysts point to their high turnover as a major reason for poor service delivery .

Johannesburg, a city of 4.8 million people that has faced water shortages for more than a week , has had 10 mayors in as many years. The neighbouring municipality of Ekurhuleni has had three mayors since 2021. To the north, in Tshwane, which contains the capital, Pretoria, the mayoralty has rotated between parties four times since 2020. In October, more than 800 people contracted a gastrointestinal illness from contaminated water in Bronkhorstspruit, in east Tshwane.

Johannesburg, Ekurhuleni and Tshwane are in Gauteng, South Africa’s most populous and densely populated province and its economic engine. The centre-right, white-led Democratic Alliance is leading the polls in all three metros but has not been polling above 40%.

The ANC’s national leadership is open to working with the DA in Gauteng, according to South African media , mirroring the government of national unity, where the two parties are the largest in the national coalition. However, local ANC leaders are reportedly not in favour of a DA tie-up. Currently, the ANC governs with a combination of the far-left Economic Freedom Fighters and the populist Patriotic Alliance and ActionSA across the province’s three metros.

In Johannesburg, the DA’s Helen Zille has led a spirited campaign, with viral stunts including the 75-year-old snorkelling in a pothole and kayaking along a flooded street. However, the former Cape Town mayor is still viewed with suspicion by many, especially black voters, due to controversial past comments appearing to excuse colonialism. Some voters also point to soaring housing costs in Cape Town , which has been run by the DA since 2006, as a reason not to vote for Zille.

The former Johannesburg DA mayor Herman Mashaba, who leads ActionSA, which is polling around 10%, has ruled out working with Zille in Johannesburg. Mashaba has called Zille a “racist”, an allegation she has always fervently denied. The ANC, for its part, has three possible mayoral candidates for the city, amid factional infighting.

In eThekwini metro, which contains the port city of Durban, the uMkhonto we Sizwe (MK) party of the former ANC president Jacob Zuma is polling above 40%. The 84-year-old Zuma, who has weathered and denied numerous corruption allegations, is set to take many of the votes of his former party, which won 42% in eThekwini in 2021 and is now polling around 10%.
sources.headline: ANC faces anger over poor services as South Africans vote in local elections

sources.body:
South Africans are voting in highly contested local elections likely to see a haemorrhaging of votes for the country's former ruling party, the African National Congress (ANC).

This year's voting season has been marked by intense campaigns that have included politicians spinning cars, watching grannies knit and even wading through giant-sized potholes.

Leaders are campaigning to head South Africa's nearly 300 municipalities, responsible for basic service provision such as water, electricity and refuse collection.

For the ANC, the elections are a chance to prove it still has what it takes to govern. The party had a disastrous showing in the last national election, when it lost its parliamentary majority for the first time since 1994 when the racist apartheid system ended.

Support for the party has been dropping significantly over the years because of anger over high levels of corruption, unemployment and crime.

At its peak, in 2004, the ANC got 70% of the vote in the general election. Two decades later its share dropped to 40%.

Polls and pundits have predicted a further loss in these elections but President Cyril Ramaphosa has denied that his party was in a downward spiral.

"What I'm seeing here is that the ANC is going higher and higher and on the 4th [of November] we will show those naysayers," he told supporters at the party's final election rally on Sunday.

In townships like Alexandra, north-east of Johannesburg, the ANC has traditionally had a strong supporter base but poor governance and voter apathy are unravelling this support.

The BBC visited the sprawling township a week before the elections and spoke to residents to get their views. One of them was Sanele Ntombela, who is a first-time voter excited to make his voice heard.

We found the 18-year-old hanging out with his friends on a street corner. Most of his friends said they had no intention of voting and had not registered to do so.

They cited a lack of change and deteriorating delivery of basic services.

But Ntombela was looking forward to voting for the first time and thought it might lead to change.

"We face many challenges in Alexandra. There's rubbish everywhere and we struggle with electricity and water and many other issues," he said.

Just metres away, heaps of rubbish lay gathered beneath a streetlight pole covered in election posters from the different political parties.

On the other side of the street, drain water trickles through the many potholes that have gutted that part of the road.

The BBC also spoke to Zandile Mncube, who said she wouldn't vote, even though she is registered to do so.

The 33-year-old woman also cited poor service delivery and performance by local leaders for her decision.

"It makes no difference [whether I vote or not]. Things have gotten worse over the years," she said.

Alex, as the township is known, is a stone's throw away from Sandton, Africa's richest square mile, but the differences could not be starker.

Sandton is known for its skyscrapers, designer shops and well-maintained roads but in Alex, houses are sandwiched together and rubbish, either piled together or left strewn across the pavement, is everywhere. The stench of raw sewage and uncollected rubbish is heavy in the air, but residents appear used to it.
sources.headline: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline

stories.headline: Bomb threats disrupt seven flights across Europe; no explosives found

sources.body:
At least seven flights and an Israel-bound cruise ship receive threats, but officials say searches found no explosives.

A series of bomb threats against passenger flights across Europe has prompted emergency searches, briefly shut down an airport outside the Polish capital, Warsaw, and led the Italian Air Force to escort a Ryanair plane into Rome.

All of the threats on Tuesday turned out to be false.

At least seven flights and an Israel-bound cruise ship were targeted, according to officials. All of the planes landed safely, and searches found no explosives.

The airlines affected included Ryanair, Wizz Air, Scandinavian Airlines and the Polish carrier LOT. Ryanair, the Irish budget carrier, appeared to be the hardest hit, with four of its flights to different destinations being targeted.

No one claimed responsibility, and officials did not attribute blame.

The incidents came a day after a plane headed for Bulgaria was diverted to Hungary after receiving a similar bomb threat while in the air.

In Poland, two Warsaw-bound flights were targeted.

Scandinavian Airlines Flight SK751 from Copenhagen landed without incident at Warsaw Chopin Airport, which closed a runway while the plane was inspected.

“The passengers disembarked, the plane landed normally; it was not an emergency landing,” Alexandra Lindgren Kaoukji, a spokesperson for the airline, told the Polish news agency PAP. She said the matter has been referred to the Polish police.

A LOT Polish Airlines flight from London’s Heathrow, which was also due at Chopin, was diverted to the city’s second airport, Warsaw Modlin, which was closed after the alert.

The plane, a Boeing 737 Max, landed safely. “Nothing was found,” said Adam Szablowski, a spokesman for Modlin. Airport officials said normal operations later resumed.

In Italy, two Eurofighter jets escorted Ryanair Flight FR9611 from Dublin into Rome’s Fiumicino Airport, where it landed at 10:45am local time, the airport’s operator said.

The Italian Air Force said it had responded immediately to “a report of a suspected threat aboard a civilian aircraft”.

An earlier Ryanair flight from Lisbon that landed at Fiumicino at 9:40am was also subjected to anti-bomb procedures. Checks of passengers, luggage and the plane “were all negative and the alert was lifted,” the operator said.

In Spain, Aena, the national airport operator, said it had activated an emergency protocol “due to a bomb alert” on a Ryanair flight from Manchester.

The plane landed in Murcia at 10:30am without incident.

In Bulgaria, a Wizz Air flight from Bergamo, Italy, was inspected after landing in the country’s capital, Sofia, a spokesperson for the Bulgarian Interior Ministry said. A Ryanair flight from Dublin to Sofia was also targeted, the country’s transport ministry said. No explosives were found on either plane.

The threats followed a similar episode on Monday, exwhen a Wizz Air flight from London’s Luton Airport to Sofia received a bomb threat in midair and was diverted to Budapest.

Hungarian Defence Minister Romulusz Ruszin-Szendi said on Facebook that NATO’s air-defence alert service had flagged the flight. He said Hungarian Gripen fighter jets “took to the air within minutes” and escorted it safely to the ground.
sources.headline: Bomb threats disrupt flights across Europe, no explosive devices found

sources.body:
Unclear if series of incidents affecting two UK departures and several Ryanair services, among others, were connected

Seven planes across Europe have been searched or diverted after a series of bomb threats were made to passenger flights, prompting questions as to whether there was any coordination behind the warnings.

Two UK departures – one from Heathrow and one from Manchester – were among those threatened in what Downing Street called “malicious hoaxes”, though all planes landed safely and no explosives were found.

A UK Department for Transport source added that the low-level threats were “not credible” and that passengers should not be concerned, though the warnings disrupted flights and prompted investigations across the UK and Europe.

None of the incidents and subsequent searches threw up any evidence of terrorist activity, though authorities were responding to an unusual number of reported threats in one day.

One of Warsaw’s two main airports, Modlin, was briefly closed after receiving a diverted plane, and Polish officials confirmed that they had received bomb threats involving two flights coming into the capital.

Italian fighter jets escorted a Ryanair plane into Rome following a warning of a suspected threat on a flight coming from Dublin. The flight landed safely and nothing untoward was reported as being found.

There was little obvious pattern surrounding the incidents, which affected flights taking off from the UK, Ireland, Denmark, Portugal and Italy, and landing in Poland, Spain, Italy and Bulgaria . Four of the flights were operated by Ryanair, the others by Wizz Air, LOT and SAS.

Investigators added there was no immediate evidence of a hostile state being behind the threats, though they continued to monitor developments, sharing information across the continent while inquiries continued.

Aviation security fears have been reignited with the recent FlyDubai incident when a co-pilot allegedly attempted to crash a Tel Aviv-bound plane. Russia has also been accused of being behind firebomb threats targeting parcel carriers using cargo planes over the past two years.

The threats followed an incident on Monday when another flight from the UK to Bulgaria was diverted, apparently without substance.

Experts said that fake threats occur on a daily basis. Philip Baum, visiting professor of aviation security at Coventry University, said: “Most are from individuals who think it is funny or want to delay a flight for some reason. If the industry was to respond to every unsubstantiated threat, flights would grind to a halt.

“The reality is that terrorist organisations who might like to smuggle a bomb on to a flight don’t tell people, they claim responsibility after the attacks.”

But he added that the fact that some aircraft did divert would “imply that the threats are credible and specific in nature, and therefore one has to respond accordingly”.

Tuesday’s series of incidents started with a flight from Heathrow operated by the Polish carrier LOT, which was scheduled to arrive at Warsaw’s Chopin airport but was diverted to the second airport, further from the Polish capital, Modlin. Authorities closed that airport after the alert and the Boeing 737 Max landed without incident.
sources.headline: Seven planes across Europe searched or diverted after ‘malicious hoax’ bomb threats

stories.headline: Greenland’s parliament approves security deal with the US and Denmark

sources.body:
Lawmakers vote 16-0 for trilateral agreement signed in September, while seven abstained.

Trump plans for ‘massive’ resource exploration in Greenland

Lawmakers in the semi-autonomous Danish territory of Greenland have approved an agreement with Denmark and the United States aimed at bolstering security in the Arctic and North Atlantic.

The deal was passed 16-0 on Tuesday, with seven lawmakers abstaining.

The agreement was signed in September by US President Donald Trump, Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen and Greenlandic Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York.

It followed months of negotiations behind the scenes amid growing tensions over Trump’s repeated threats to seize the vast, resource-rich Arctic island.

Greenlandic Foreign Minister Mute Egede said the ratification was another important step for the self-governing island.

“The road to this point has been ⁠a difficult one for us as ⁠a people. But we have stood firm on our fundamental principles, chosen dialogue and taken responsibility for our country’s interests,” he wrote in a ⁠post on Facebook.

“This is about all of us. The Greenland we love. ⁠About our security. And about our ⁠right to shape our own future,” he said.

Located between Europe and North America, Greenland is the world’s largest island, with a population of 57,000 people.

Trump’s refusal last year to rule out a military invasion had caused fear among Greenlanders, the majority of whom rejected US control, according to opinion polls.

The trilateral deal paves the way for more US bases on Greenland. It also allows the US to “modernise and expand” its activities at the Pituffik Space Base, a remote US military installation in northwest Greenland.

Under its terms, Greenland will remain under Danish control – but the agreement would still apply if the island eventually chooses independence.

The deal stipulates it will only “enter into force” once the “necessary parliamentary processes of the Kingdom of Denmark, in conjunction with Greenland, have been completed”.

Danish lawmakers are set to debate it later this month, while no approval is required from the US Senate.
sources.headline: Greenland parliament approves security deal with US, Denmark

stories.headline: Brazil publishes global roadmap for phasing out fossil fuels

sources.body:
Cop30 host sets out steps to break link with coal, oil and gas as it aims to move focus from negotiating to implementing

All countries can start to break their dependence on fossil fuels now without needing to wait for new technologies or economic changes, Brazil’s government has said ahead of a global climate summit.

Brazil, the host of last year’s UN climate conference , set out the world’s first global “roadmap” for phasing out fossil fuels on Tuesday, showing that countries could boost their economies and pull people out of poverty while breaking the link with coal, oil and gas.

But Joeri Rogelj, a professor of climate science and policy at Imperial College London, said that although the Brazilian roadmaps represented a step forward, they were limited. “The roadmaps are valuable but fall short of clearly indicating the pace of change needed by including no timeline or key benchmarks,” he said.

“Because of this omission, they still leave much to be imagined about what is needed to achieve the Paris agreement’s ultimate goal: limiting global warming to well below 2C, and preferably to 1.5C, to avoid dangerous climate harm.”

André Corrêa do Lago, Brazil’s president of the Cop30 summit, said the roadmaps were intended to help move the annual UN Cops away from their previous focus on negotiating global agreements to tackle the climate crisis, and on to implementing the targets that had already been agreed. Cop31 takes place in Antalya, Turkey, this month.

“They are documents of implementation,” Corrêa do Lago told the Guardian in an interview. “There is a different group of people that negotiate and that implement. The problem we’ve had at many Cops is to think that the same people who negotiate might also need to coordinate the implementation – this is not the case.”

He said the roadmaps should be taken up by ministries of finance, transportation, energy and infrastructure to work on how they could be implemented in each country.

Brazil hosted the Cop30 summit last November in the coastal city of Belém, in the Amazon rainforest, where a bitter dispute broke out over whether the final set of resolutions should include pledges on fossil fuels. As a compromise, the presidency agreed to produce two roadmaps, one on “transitioning away from fossil fuels in energy systems in a just orderly and equitable manner” and the other on halting and reversing deforestation.

These roadmaps are separate from similarly named plans from governments that met after Cop30 at a conference in Santa Marta , Colombia, in April, to discuss the transition away from fossil fuels. At that conference, nearly 60 countries formed a new “coalition of the willing”, separate to Cops, to set out their own national roadmaps to phase out fossil fuels. Several countries have since produced national plans , including Germany, France and the Netherlands.

The roadmaps produced by governments under the Santa Marta initiative are much more specific and prescriptive than Brazil’s, as each of those is written by the national government responsible for implementing the policies recommended.
sources.headline: Brazil publishes first global ‘roadmap’ for phasing out fossil fuels

stories.headline: Spain’s transport minister resigns after two deadly train crashes

sources.body:
El ministro de Transportes, Óscar Puente, ha dimitido tras los dos gravísimos accidentes registrados en la alta velocidad española en el último año. El ministro ha anunciado su decisión en el último turno de palabra de la Diputación Permanente del Congreso, donde llevaba compareciendo desde las 17.00 para explicar lo sucedido en el último siniestro, el de Urda, que se ha saldado con 69 muertos y decenas de heridos. Puente además ha precisado que tampoco será el cabeza de lista del PSOE por Valladolid en las elecciones generales.

"La decisión la tomé los primeros minutos en los que se produjo la tragedia. Según me dirigía al centro de Adif se lo hice saber, en primer lugar, a mi familia. Un ministro no puede continuar en su cargo con dos accidentes de esta gravedad en menos de un año. Es una cuestión de dignidad política, por coherencia y empatía política". Así ha empezado su última intervención Puente, que ha explicado que no ha querido anunciar su decisión hasta que no hubiese "cumplido" con una cuestión inaplazable: "Garantizar la seguridad [de la red ferroviaria] en el corto plazo".

Sus siguientes palabras han sido para aquellas personas que le han apoyado estos días. A estos les ha trasladado que su dimisión "es una medida necesaria y positiva. No es ningún drama. Drama el de las víctimas, el de sus familias, sus seres queridos, que no van a poder volver. Sé que mi dolor no puede equipararse al suyo, pero después del suyo, créanme, ninguno es tan grande como el mío", ha continuado Puente, visiblemente emocionado.

El ya exministro ha recurrido a una frase de Jorge Coelho, político portugués que en 2001, tras el derrumbe del puente Puente Hintze Ribeiro en el que murieron 59 personas, utilizó una frase que el socialista ha hecho suya esta tarde: "La culpa no puede morir soltera". Puente, que hasta ahora había rechazado dimitir excusándose en que su labor era la de esclarecer lo sucedido y ofrecer todas las explicaciones posibles, ha defendido que su marcha "es buena para el país, para la democracia, una democracia madura, de un país fuerte, próspero y moderno. Una democracia en la que la ciudadanía reclama dignidad y mi único propósito es dársela".

Por último, ha cerrado su intervención con unas palabras de agradecimiento hacia el presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, y con un llamamiento para que la gente respalde el proyecto de los socialistas. "Gracias al PSOE, a mis compañeros del Ayuntamiento, a mi equipo y, muy especialmente, a Pedro Sánchez por su confianza sin límite. Sé que este será un momento triste para él , uno más en este camino de luces y sombras que es la vida y la política. Animo a todos los progresistas de este país a ayudarle. Se lo merece. Ayudándole a él nos ayudamos todos", ha remarcado.

Tan sólo unos minutos antes, el ministro había cargado con dureza contra la portavoz del PP, Ester Muñoz, que había exigido su dimisión. " Señora Muñoz, sé que dar explicaciones no es suficiente , por supuesto no sirve para consolar ni paliar el daño que las víctimas han sufrido, pero es cumplir con mi deber más elemental y es más de lo que cualquiera de ustedes han hecho en cualquiera de las catástrofes que han tenido que enfrentar", reprochó Puente, que en su primera alocución, de tono institucional, se había ceñido, prácticamente, a recordar la cronología del accidente y a enumerar las medidas que el Consejo de Ministros ha aprobado este martes para evitar otro siniestro como el de Urda.

sources.body:
Óscar Puente also announces his withdrawal from upcoming election following disaster that killed 69 people

Spain’s transport minister handed in his resignation on Tuesday after the train crash that killed 69 people last week, one of the worst railway disasters in Europe this century.

Óscar Puente, who had earlier pledged to work “tirelessly” to restore confidence in the world’s second-largest high-speed rail network, also said he was withdrawing from the country’s upcoming general election.

Last week’s crash, and another disaster earlier this year , have overshadowed campaigning for the 29 November ballot, in which the Socialist prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, is trailing in opinion polls.

Puente had ruled out resigning on several occasions since the disaster.

But at the end of a lengthy hearing before lawmakers, he said: “I wish to inform you that I am not only stepping down from my position as minister of transport, but that I am also withdrawing my name from the lists for the early legislative elections on 29 November.”

Hours earlier, at a press conference during which he presented measures to improve safety, the minister had said the government would “work tirelessly to achieve and regain the public’s trust in high-speed rail”.

The rightwing opposition, which had demanded Puente’s resignation, and unions had criticised him for appearing to pin all the blame for the disaster on one control centre operator.

The crash happened when a train operated by the state-owned company Renfe ploughed into the back of a stationary train belonging to the private Spanish operator Iryo on Wednesday outside the village of Urda, about 80 miles south of Madrid.

The failure of an automatic safety system halted all trains on a 39-mile stretch of track, but a control centre nonetheless authorised the Renfe service to resume its journey.

Among the measures announced at the earlier press conference by Puente was the creation of software for control centres that would issue automatic alerts and make it easier to spot anomalies in traffic.

Puente said an AI agent would be created to oversee the system and “minimise the possibility of human error”, describing the proposal as unprecedented.

In scenarios where a control centre operator took a decision while the automatic safety system was down, a second operator would have to confirm it, Puente added.

A digest of the morning's main headlines from the Europe edition emailed direct to you every week day

The train drivers’ union Semaf, which has called strikes at Renfe for 10 and 12 November, has denounced a worsening of working conditions and the use of “degraded systems”.

Critics say investment in maintenance has not kept up with the increase in passenger numbers since the 2021 liberalisation of Spain’s rail network, which allowed private companies to break Renfe’s decades-long monopoly.

In an apparent recognition of the unions’ demands, Puente said the working conditions of control centre operators would be reformed, including their breaks and by monitoring their fatigue levels.
sources.headline: Spanish transport minister resigns after deadly train crash

sources.body: (ACN) Els comitès d’empresa d’Adif i Renfe convocaran una vaga conjunta a les empreses ferroviàries públiques el dimarts 17 de novembre per reclamar millores de seguretat al sistema ferroviari. L’aturada es fa com a resposta al xoc de trens d’alta velocitat d’Urda el 28 d’octubre amb un balanç de 69 morts . Prèviament, els sindicats que formen part dels comitès han organitzat una concentració dels treballadors d’Adif i Renfe davant el Congrés dels Diputats el 16 de novembre , un dia abans de la vaga. També et pot interessar SEMAF convoca dos nous dies de vaga abans i després de l’11-N: el 10 i el 12 de novembre Marta Casals Torres 4 minuts de lectura Els sindicats demanen canvis En aquest context de mobilitzacions, la UGT traslladarà aquestes mateixes dates del 16 i 17 de novembre a la resta d’empreses del sector ferroviari per aconseguir una vaga sectorial. Per la seva banda, CCOO considera que la separació de Renfe i Adif va ser “un error” i reclama la constitució d’un grup públic d’empreses que recuperi la coordinació entre la infraestructura i l’operació ferroviària . També et pot interessar El Govern espanyol estudia aturar l’alta velocitat Madrid-Barcelona per fer-hi obres de millora Andrea Muñoz 3 minuts de lectura CCOO considera que la situació actual és el resultat del fracàs d’un model ferroviari imposat progressivament a través de les diferents directives europees, que ha afavorit la fragmentació del sistema. Per això, el sindicat també reclama la revisió dels protocols de seguretat a Adif i Renfe , plantilles suficients i formades adequadament i el reforç de la prevenció de riscos laborals i dels plans d’emergència. També et pot interessar Puente diu que no hi ha cap decisió presa sobre aturar l’alta velocitat Madrid-Barcelona Redaccio Societat Sandra García Prat 1 minut de lectura Alferro denuncia Óscar Puente En paral·lel, el sindicat Alferro ha denunciat el ministre de Transports, Óscar Puente , a la Fiscalia del Tribunal Suprem per les filtracions dels àudios del centre de control que es van publicar el mateix dia del sinistre als mitjans. En un missatge a la xarxa X, l’organització sindical ha exigit una “investigació rigorosa” i “sense anticipar conclusions” que assenyalin els treballadors. També et pot interessar 68 morts i 58 ferits en un accident entre dos trens d’alta velocitat a Toledo Marta Casals Torres 4 minuts de lectura

sources.body:
Pedro Marco de la Peña, presidente de Adif

El comité de empresa del gestor ferroviario Adif, conformado por CCOO, UGT, CGT, el Sindicato Ferroviario (SF) y el Sindicato de Circulación Ferroviario (SCF), ha acordado este martes una huelga para el próximo 17 de noviembre, aunque todavía no está convocada de manera formal, han confirmado a EFE distintas fuentes sindicales.

Las mismas fuentes destacan que esta propuesta de huelga, motivada por las inquietudes sindicales en cuanto a la seguridad ferroviaria del sistema español, también se ha trasladado al comité de empresa de Renfe para ese mismo martes.

Desde Semaf subrayan que, por el momento, no hay información al respecto, mientras que fuentes de CCOO recalcan que el anuncio del parón en Renfe todavía se está cerrando.

Por su parte, el Sindicato de Circulación Ferroviario (SCF) asegura que la convocatoria de Adif se ha acordado durante una reunión del comité de empresa celebrada este martes, en la que también se ha pactado una concentración el próximo lunes 16 de noviembre.

Además, el miércoles 18 habrá una nueva reunión del comité de empresa para analizar la evolución de la situación y valorar nuevas acciones, indicaron las fuentes.

Esta convocatoria, si nada lo evita, las movilizaciones que el sindicato Semaf tirará adelante para los días 10, con un paro total, y 12 de noviembre, con una huelga parcial, tal y como anunció el pasado 29 de octubre. Los maquinistas reclaman resolver los problemas de fiabilidad de la red ferroviaria, protocolos claros ante fenómenos meteorológicos adversos, ampliación de plantilla, mejoras en la comunicación en el caso de que se produzcan emergencias, nuevas promociones de conductores de tren, la correcta aplicación de los tiempos de conducción y la atención psicológica a los profesionales tras producirse un arrollamiento. Durante la huelga del pasado jueves, en Rodalies se registró una caída de la demanda del 30%.

sources.body: <p>La profunda brecha ideológica que divide al mundo se ha colado también en la negociación de la declaración conjunta de la XXX Cumbre Iberoamericana, que se celebra este miércoles y jueves en Madrid. Finalmente España, anfitriona de esta edición, ha logrado salvar los muebles de una cumbre con más ausencias de las previstas, a la que <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-03/las-ausencias-de-lula-y-sheinbaum-dejan-solo-a-sanchez-frente-a-milei-en-la-cumbre-iberoamericana-de-madrid.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-03/las-ausencias-de-lula-y-sheinbaum-dejan-solo-a-sanchez-frente-a-milei-en-la-cumbre-iberoamericana-de-madrid.html">han dado plantón los principales mandatarios progresistas, como la mexicana Claudia Sheinbaum o el brasileño Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.</a> Pese a ello, los negociadores alcanzaron este martes un principio de acuerdo en torno a un texto de mínimos que debe ser ratificado por los jefes de las delegaciones de los 22 países de lengua española o portuguesa de Europa y América. No es un logro menor, ya que la anterior cumbre, celebrada en Cuenca (Ecuador), se cerró por primera vez en 33 años sin una declaración final. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-04/espana-salva-el-consenso-iberoamericano-con-una-declaracion-final-de-minimos.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

stories.headline: Supreme Court judge closes investigation against Puigdemont, Comín and Puig, paving the way for amnesty

sources.body:
El exconseller Lluís Puig (derecha), junto al expresident Carles Puigdemont (centro) y el exconseller Toni Comín (izquierda). ACN / Maria Garcia

El juez Pablo Llarena ha cerrado el sumario abierto desde 2017 contra el expresident Carles Puigdemont y los exconsellers Toni Comín y Lluís Puig por el procés, último paso para que la Sala de lo Penal del Tribunal Supremo le aplique definitivamente la amnistía y le exima de toda responsabilidad penal.

Según el auto conocido este martes y al que ha tenido acceso RTVE, Llarena ha declarado "concluso el sumario respecto de los tres encausados y remitir las actuaciones a la Sala de lo Penal de este Tribunal Supremo para que resuelva sobre la finalización de la fase de instrucción y un eventual sobreseimiento libre de las actuaciones por aplicación de la Ley de amnistía, con emplazamiento de las partes en los términos legales".

La portavoz de Junts en el Congreso de los Diputados, Miriam Nogueras , ha celebrado en declaraciones a los medios lo que ha descrito una "muy buena noticia". Ahora, confía en que esta "victoria del independentismo y de Carles Puigdemont", como ha descrito la amnistía, termine de aplicarse y que se haga "de manera inmediata".

Con los otros líderes independentistas, entre ellos el presidente de ERC, Oriol Junqueras , ya amnistiados, no queda ningún obstáculo para que la Sala de lo Penal del Supremo aplique la ley para Puigdemont, que puede volver a España desde hace semanas dado que su orden de detención fue levantada.

Llarena entendió ya hace semanas que la doctrina sobre la concesión de la amnistía al delito de malversación fijada en la sentencia del Tribunal Constitucional que concedió el amparo a la exconsejera Dolors Bassa era extensible al caso del expresidente catalán.

Asimismo, desestimó el recurso presentado por la acusación popular de Vox contra su decisión de dejar sin efecto las órdenes de detención contra Puigdemont, Comín y Puig, los tres miembros del Govern que estaban procesados y que no fueron juzgados tras huir de la justicia.

sources.body:
Pablo Llarena ha fet, ara sí, el pas que faltava perquè el Suprem amnistiï l'expresident Carles Puigdemont i els exconsellers Lluís Puig i Toni Comín. Resolts els recursos pendents, el jutge ha tancat la causa contra el president Puigdemont i l'ha enviat a la sala segona del Suprem .

L'últim pas que queda és que el Suprem arxivi definitivament el cas i els apliqui l'amnistia després de 9 anys d'exili a Bèlgica.

Després d'haver deixat sense efecte l'ordre de detenció que pesava sobre ells si trepitjaven territori espanyol, el jutge del Tribunal Suprem ha decidit tancar la causa i l'envia a la sala segona del Suprem per aplicar-los plenament l'amnistia que el Congrés va aprovar fa gairebé dos anys i mig .

Ho fa a contracor , com ja va voler deixar clar el dia que va confirmar la retirada de les ordres de detenció contra els tres exiliats, dient que acceptava aplicar la decisió del Constitucional encara que no compartia els motius en què es basava.

Aleshores, Llarena es va resistir a tancar la causa al·legant que encara quedaven recursos per resoldre i que era la Sala del Tribunal Suprem qui s'havia de pronunciar sobre la conclusió del cas.

En una atenció als mitjans al Congrés aquest dimarts, la portaveu de Junts al Congrés , Míriam Nogueras, ha demanat al Suprem que apliqui aquesta amnistia "de manera immediata" i ha qualificat la interlocutòria de Llarena de "molt bona notícia", tot i que ha insistit a dir que "encara falta el darrer pas".

En l'escrit d'aquest dimarts, el jutge deixa clar que considera que "subsisteixen els indicis de participació" de Puigdemont, Comín i Puig en "l'organització i finançament amb fons públics del referèndum de l'1 d'octubre del 2017", però admet que la llei d'amnistia i la interpretació que n'ha fet el Constitucional "impedeixen mantenir-ne el processament".

El magistrat explica que "la impossibilitat de continuar la persecució penal" no deriva "ni d'una despenalització de la malversació, ni de la desaparició dels indicis que van sustentar el processament contra els encausats", "sinó de la decisió legislativa d'amnistiar les concretes conductes investigades i de l'abast atribuït a aquesta decisió per la majoria del Tribunal Constitucional".

Per tant, "procedeix deixar sense efecte el processament, declarar conclòs el sumari respecte d'aquests encausats i remetre'l a la Sala perquè resolgui sobre la finalització de la fase d'instrucció i l'eventual sobreseïment lliure de les actuacions per aplicació de la llei d'amnistia".

La decisió de Llarena posa punt i final al seu periple per intentar asseure al banc dels acusats Carles Puigdemont i els exconsellers del seu govern.

Quan va assumir el cas, Llarena va decidir retirar la primera euroordre que hi havia contra Puigdemont i la part del govern de l'exili. Ho va fer per evitar que la justícia belga limités els delictes pels quals es podria entregar Puigdemont.

Després va declarar en rebel·lia processal Puigdemont , el 23 de març del 2018, i va decretar la segona ordre de detenció nacional i internacional. La va retirar després que Alemanya limités les condicions d'extradició de Puigdemont.
sources.headline: Llarena tanca la causa contra Puigdemont, Comín i Puig, que queden a un pas de l'amnistia definitiva

stories.headline: Judge investigating alleged Barcelona unrest organiser orders him held in custody

sources.body:
Un juez de Barcelona ha considerado la red Blocus un " grupo criminal " y ha enviado a prisión provisional y sin fianza a uno de sus presuntos cabecillas, según se desprende de un auto al que ha tenido acceso RTVE Catalunya. En un registro en su domicilio se hallaron dos catanas y un arma de fuego . Hasta ahora son ya 16 los detenidos por su supuesta participación en grupos organizados que incitaban a desórdenes y saqueos en varias ciudades de España.

El investigado, nacido en España y de 18 años, carece de antecedentes penales y, según el magistrado José Villodre López, del Juzgado 1 de Instancia e Instrucción de Barcelona, podría ser responsable, al menos, de un delito de conspiración para la comisión de un delito de desórdenes públicos y otro de pertenencia a grupo criminal en su modalidad agravada.

Ya son 16 los detenidos por su participación en Blocus, los grupos organizados que incitaban a desórdenes y saqueos en varias ciudades de España. En Barcelona, el juez ha enviado a prisión a ...

El juez especifica que en los días previos al pasado 24 de octubre, a través de la plataforma Blocus, se incitó a la participación violenta en una manifestación que discurriría por las calles de la ciudad condal. A través de un código QR inserto en la propia convocatoria los interesados fueron integrándose en distintos grupos de Whatsapp y Telegram donde se daban "instrucciones concretas" sobre lugares de encuentro, vestimenta y forma de proceder. Uno de esos grupos se denominaba “Joyerías Bcn 24 de octubre” y estaba liderado presuntamente por el joven ahora arrestado.

Con frases como: "Lo petamos todo" o "no tengáis piedad de nadie" , el joven incitaba supuestamente en los chats a la participación violenta.

"Como consecuencia de este proceder centenares de personas sumieron el centro de Barcelona en el caos : 33 barricadas incendiadas o 23 establecimientos violentados tras reventar las puertas de acceso y las cristaleras. El saldo de detenidos fue de 135", agrega el auto.

La causa judicial que dirige este Tribunal tiene por objetivo investigar esos incidentes, que partían de una previa convocatoria "focalizada en la comisión de actos vandálicos".

Los roles de los implicados, señala el auto, "estaban bien delimitados: ideólogos de la convocatoria, dinamizadores de los distintos grupos con instrucciones precisas sobre vestimenta u objetivos y, finalmente, los ejecutores materiales". E indica que el joven podría estar "en el primer o segundo eslabón" . "Amén de los textos incitando a la violencia sin contemplaciones, no pasa desapercibido el envío de un plano con el lugar de encuentro, instrucciones que solo puede ofrecer quien lidera o dirige y no un mero subalterno", remarca el juez.

Y enfatiza que no se puede descartar que participara "personal y directamente" en los incendios, daños o actos de pillaje.

En su declaración , el joven rechazó cualquier tipo de responsabilidad achacándola a los mensajes, una "suerte de respuesta a las provocaciones que sobre su pasividad le habían hecho sus amigos". Pero el juez considera que no hay ningún elemento que valide esta "excusa".

sources.body:
El jove detingut a Picanya, al País Valencià , com a "presumpte fundador i principal impulsor" de Blocus a l'Estat va viatjar a París uns dies abans, segons apunta la investigació preliminar.

Així es desprèn de la interlocutòria judicial, en què la magistrada assegura que " hi ha set indicis , sis de grau elevat , per creure que és la persona que operava sota la identitat FUCK A.E.A.T.".

Precisament, aquest era l'àlies del creador i administrador dels grups més nombrosos de Blocus a Barcelona, de fins a dos milers d'integrants.

El detingut està en presó provisional comunicada i sense fiança , acusat dels delictes d' organització criminal destinada a la mobilització per cometre desordres públics greus , robatoris amb força en comerços i danys dolosos .

Al detingut se li van decomissar dos dispositius mòbils i dos ordinadors , que han estat elements destacats de la investigació.

En un dels telèfons de l'acusat, hi havia les sessions obertes de dos grups de captació d'integrants . També s'hi va trobar un enllaç trampa amb l'identificador del seu compte de Telegram, enviat des del seu WhatsApp personal.

Els investigadors asseguren que els cartells de les convocatòries de "Blocus 3 BCN", "Blocus 4 Barcelona" i "31 d'octubre" van ser encarregats a una IA des d'aquest dispositiu.

Els missatges que enviava a través d'aquests grups "fixaven un pla orientat al saqueig de comerços de luxe sense presència policial", afirma la magistrada.

També li atribueixen l'autoria del "vídeo revelació", que va difondre ell uns dies abans de la detenció, i que va ser enregistrat i editat també amb el mateix telèfon mòbil decomissat.

En aquest vídeo, el detingut apareixia encaputxat i amb la veu distorsionada. Parlava en nom de Blocus i convocava a repetir els aldarulls del dia 24 d'octubre.

En el document, s'afirma que hi ha indicis per creure que el detingut dirigia "una estructura estable", "amb repartiment de funcions, fet que podria constituir un delicte d'organització criminal".

Afegeix que era ell qui seleccionava personalment els integrants del nucli tancat de l'organització –a banda dels grups de Telegram– i que va captar un menor de 17 anys.

No es descarten noves detencions, perquè falten per identificar altres integrants del grup, com l'assessor de seguretat i els membres del comitè que va assumir el control després de la seva detenció el 30 d'octubre.

La jutgessa justifica la petició de la presó provisional sense fiança per "la gravetat de la pena, possibilitat de reiteració delictiva i el risc de fuga" .

De fet, segons el material informàtic decomissat i ell mateix va reconèixer durant la compareixença, " s'hauria desplaçat a París , ciutat en la qual, com és públicament conegut, es van iniciar els disturbis organitzats de gravíssimes conseqüències".

A més, aquesta mesura cautelar permetria evitar "la reiteració delictiva per la facilitat que ha mostrat de mobilitzar grups de persones, sobretot de menors d'edat ".
sources.headline: El presumpte líder de Blocus va viatjar a París abans d'impulsar els aldarulls a Barcelona

stories.headline: Barcelona housing protesters plan to remain in Plaça de Catalunya through the election

sources.body: L’acampada pel dret a l’habitatge de la plaça de Catalunya s’ha mobilitzat aquest dimarts a la tarda per condemnar el desallotjament de l’acampada de Madrid . Malgrat la pluja, una trentena de persones s’ha concentrat davant del monument de Francesc Macià a la mateixa plaça per mostrar la solidaritat amb les persones desallotjades a la protesta madrilenya. En aquest sentit, els acampats asseguren que la idea és resistir a la plaça de Catalunya fins després de les eleccions generals del 29 de novembre per defensar el dret a un habitatge digne per a tothom. També et pot interessar Collboni no desallotjarà l’acampada d’habitatge, però avisa: la GUB està preparada per actuar si cal Roger Torres i Liñán 1 minut de lectura Un desallotjament de matinada El desallotjament de l’acampada de Madrid , a la Puerta del Sol, s’ha produït aquesta matinada. En total s’han desallotjat 334 persones i s’han detingut dues persones per desobediència i resistència. Per tot això, els acampats a Barcelona han mostrat la seva preocupació que aquesta actuació comenci una cadena de desallotjaments de campaments arreu de l’estat, incloent el d’aquí. De moment, des de l’acampada indiquen que no han rebut cap notificació de ningú per marxar . També et pot interessar Membres de l’acampada i de sindicats d’habitatge ocupen un edifici buit a l’Eixample Andrea Muñoz Maria Solans Marina Sancho 2 minuts de lectura
sources.headline: Protesta a Barcelona per condemnar el desallotjament de l’acampada per l’habitatge de Madrid

stories.headline: Cristina Fernández Cubas wins the 2026 Cervantes Prize

sources.body: (ACN) L’escriptora i periodista Cristina Fernández Cubas ha estat distingida amb el Premi Cervantes 2026 , segons ha anunciat el ministre de Cultura, Ernest Urtasun. Llicenciada en Dret i Periodisme a Barcelona i casada amb l’escriptor Carlos Trías Sagner, és autora de contes i novel·les que li han valgut guardons com el Premi Ciutat de Barcelona el 2009 i el Premi Nacional de Narrativa de les Lletres Espanyoles el 2023. Urtasun ha estat l’encarregat de llegir la decisió del jurat, que ha destacat “l’originalitat, excel·lència i coherència d’una obra que ha renovat el conte contemporani i ha transformat la literatura fantàstica en espanyol” i que la situa com una de les figures “més importants” de les lletres hispàniques. El jurat també ha destacat la trajectòria “sòlida” de la guardonada, que ha contribuït “decisivament” a revalorar el relat breu “reivindicant-lo com una forma d’expressió autònoma capaç d’assolir la màxima intensitat estètica i profunditat existencials”. També et pot interessar Eva Baltasar guanya el prestigiós premi Médicis Étranger Clara Vera Colina 1 minut de lectura Ha publicat una vintena d’obres Nascuda a Arenys de Mar el 1945 i resident a Barcelona, Fernández Cubas va publicar el primer volum de contes, La meva germana Elba , el 1980. Des d’aleshores ha publicat una vintena d’obres. “A través d’una precisió narrativa impecable, el domini absolut del punt de vista i l’administració dels silencis —ha llegit Urtasun—, les seves històries es converteixen en experiències perdurables que interpel·len directament el lector i desestabilitzen les seves certeses en descobrir l’inquietant en el quotidià i qüestionar els límits de la realitat, la identitat i el coneixement”. També et pot interessar Enrique Vila-Matas, Premi Nacional de les Lletres Espanyoles 2026 Esther Castarnado 1 minut de lectura
sources.headline: L’escriptora i periodista barcelonina Cristina Fernández Cubas, Premi Cervantes 2026

sources.body:
La catalana Cristina Fernández Cubas ha estat la guanyadora del Premi Cervantes . Dotat amb 125.000 euros, es considera el guardó oficial més prestigiós de la llengua castellana. Nascuda a Arenys de Mar el 1945, Fernández Cubas, escriptora i periodista, és una de les plomes més destacades a l'hora de crear contes i relats breus en la literatura espanyola de les dècades del 1990 i el 2000.

El jurat del premi ha destacat l'autora, precisament, per "l'originalitat, l'excel·lència i la coherència d'una obra que ha renovat el conte contemporani i ha transformat la literatura fantàstica ". El seu treball, a més, "representa una aportació fonamental" que la consagra "com una de les figures més importants de les lletres hispàniques".

Va estudiar Dret i Periodisme i, el 1980, amb el recull de contes "Mi hermana Elba", es va donar a conèixer literàriament com una escriptora capaç de convertir situacions quotidianes en experiències inquietants. "Los altillos de Brumal" (1983) va suposar una consolidació i, alhora, un aprofundiment en el seu univers fantàstic.

Posteriorment vindrien "El ángulo del horror" (1990), "Con Agatha en Estambul" (1994) i "Parientes pobres del diablo" (2006), amb el qual va guanyar el Premi Setenil al millor llibre de relats publicat a Espanya.

La recopilació de la majoria dels seus títols publicada el 2008 sota el títol "Todos los cuentos" va rebre el Premi Ciutat de Barcelona de literatura en llengua castellana, el desaparegut Premi Salambó de narrativa en castellà i el Premio Cálamo al llibre de l'any. Amb un altre llibre de relats, "La habitación de Nona" (2015), va obtenir el Premi de la Crítica, el Premi Dulce Chacón i el Premi Nacional de Narrativa del Ministeri de Cultura.

Tot i l'àmplia producció d'obres de relat breu, també ha escrit novel·les com "El año de Gracia" (1985), "El columpio" (1995) i "La puerta entreabierta" (2013), amb el pseudònim Fernanda Kubbs.

A més, és autora de l'obra de teatre "Hermanas de sangre" (1998), adaptada com a pel·lícula, "Germanes de sang" , per TV3. També va firmar el llibre de memòries "Cosas que ya no existen" (2001) i l'assaig "Emilia Pardo Bazán" (2001).

Fernández Cubas ha editat bona part de la seva obra a l'editorial barcelonina Tusquets , on l'any passat publicava "Lo que no se ve" , en què jugava amb tot allò que és inexplicable. Explicar els silencis, el que no es diu, el que només intuïm, és una de les seves especialitats.

L'any 2023 se li va concedir el Premi Nacional de les Lletres Espanyoles per la "màgia de la seva narrativa, que l'ha portat a ser considerada una de les millors contistes espanyoles".

L'autora és la setena dona a rebre el Cervantes ; la darrera va ser la uruguaiana Cristina Peri Rossi el 2021. L'any passat el guardó es va concedir a l'escriptor mexicà Gonzalo Celorio i l'anterior a Álvaro Pombo, mantenint l'alternança de continents en la procedència dels premiats.
sources.headline: Premi Cervantes 2026 a la catalana Cristina Fernández Cubas, mestra del conte i el relat breu

stories.headline: Spain commits €3.9 million to monastery renovation for the future Thyssen museum in Sant Feliu de Guíxols

sources.body:
Vista aèria del monestir de Sant Feliu de Guíxols. / Ajuntament de Sant Feliu de Guíxols

L'Estat aportarà 3,9 milions d'euros per reformar el monestir de Sant Feliu de Guíxols que acollirà el futur Museu Thyssen. El govern espanyol ha donat a conèixer aquest dimarts el llistat provisional de projectes que es veuran beneficiats de les ajudes del 2% Cultural. Són 78 edificis històrics i el monestir ganxó serà el segon que rebrà més aportació per darrere del de Santa Catalina de Siena de Valladolid (4,22 MEUR). El Museu Thyssen de Sant Feliu de Guíxols, que acollirà obres de la pinacoteca catalana de la baronessa, preveu obrir portes a mitjans del 2028. L'Ajuntament ja ha licitat la primera fase de les obres, que sumen 9,1 milions, i que es preveuen engegar a finals d'aquest any o principis del 2027.

El programa del 2% Cultural neix de l'obligació que tenen els Ministeris d'Habitatge, de Transports i de Cultura de destinar aquest percentatge de les seves partides d'obra pública a impulsar la conservació del patrimoni històric. A l'última convocatòria s'hi van presentar 422 projectes.

Ara, la comissió mixta per al Programa 2% Cultural ja ha aprovat el llistat provisional de projectes que se'n veuran beneficiats. En total, segons ha donat a conèixer el govern espanyol, són 78 monuments que en conjunt rebran subvencions per valor de 80 MEUR.

A Catalunya, el 2% Cultural destinarà ajudes per valor d'11,7 milions d'euros. I gairebé una tercera part d'aquest global anirà a parar a Sant Feliu de Guíxols. Perquè el projecte de reforma del monestir, que acollirà el futur Museu Thyssen, rebrà una aportació de 3,9 MEUR. És la segona més elevada de tots els monuments que formen part del llistat, per darrere del monestir de Santa Catalina de Siena de Valladolid (4,22 MEUR).

El futur Museu Thyssen de Sant Feliu de Guíxols ha d'acollir obres de pintura catalana de la col·lecció de la baronessa. L'Ajuntament ja ha licitat la primera fase de les obres de reforma de l'interior del monestir, que sumen 9,1 milions dels 12,9 que costarà el projecte. Es preveu que els treballs comencin a finals d'aquest any o a principis del vinent i que tinguin un termini d'execució de divuit mesos, amb l'objectiu que el museu obri portes a mitjans del 2028.

El futur Thyssen de Sant Feliu de Guíxols s'emmarca dins el projecte global del Monestir de les Arts que, a banda del museu, també tindrà una pota educativa i d'interpretació del mateix monestir. En aquesta primera fase de les obres, l'Ajuntament hi aportarà 2,1 MEUR. La resta, vindran d'altres administracions i entitats.

Els treballs se centraran en reformar l'interior de l'edifici i permetran posar en funcionament tant el Museu Thyssen com la resta de sales d'exposicions. Aquesta primera fase de l'obra contempla 6,2 milions per a l'adequació de l'edifici i 1,2 milions per a l'edificació de l'entorn. Segons va explicar aquest setembre el consistori, l'emblemàtic cub del vestíbul d'accés que s'havia d'aixecar al pati de l'Abadia quedarà per a una segona fase.
sources.headline: L'Estat aporta 3,9 milions per reformar el monestir de Sant Feliu de Guíxols que acollirà el Museu Thyssen
